question: At the same card count, which accelerator trains this model faster per point spent?
why_earlier_numbers_did_not_answer_it: Every Ascend measurement before today was 16 cards on one node, so it never paid for a cross-node allreduce, while the L40S numbers it was compared against always did.
Both sides were host-bound by a corpus-reader defect (below), so they measured the reader rather than the accelerator.

configuration.recompute: full backbone and DiT, 6 retained full-attention activations

corpus_reader_defect.symptom: image_wait_share 0.92 in the packer thread; no thread setting moved it (torch intra-op threads: no effect, doubling image workers: +3.5%).
corpus_reader_defect.cause: corpus_pipeline/production/portable_refs.py read_ref_bytes SHA256-hashed the entire containing TAR on first touch of each archive.
corpus_reader_defect.fix: Stream the member and keep its own SHA256, declared length and open-file stat check, which is what pins the bytes. The whole-archive hash attests to the container, not the data; release acceptance keeps it (default unchanged), training reads skip it.
corpus_reader_defect.integrity_retained: tests/test_archive_verification.py: corrupted bytes, wrong member hash, wrong size and out-of-range extents are all still rejected; both modes return identical bytes.

varlen_attention_ab.what: One packed varlen call replaces the per-visual attention loop in the Wan DiT and the vision tower. Same global batch, same loader, same job; PRETRAIN_{CUDA,NPU}_VARLEN=0 restores the loop, which is also the numerical oracle.
varlen_attention_ab.numerics_gate: Passed on both backends against an FP64 CPU oracle: forward bit-identical on Ascend, gradient disagreement at most 2.7e-05 against a BF16 self-error of ~0.004.

ascend_32_cards.gain: +10.8 percent; both arms fully fed, so this is device-side
ascend_32_cards.probe_is_valid_here: Ascend shows no warm-up: steps 2-20 sit in 14.9-17.2 s with no trend.

l40s_32_cards.finding: varlen does not help on CUDA and may cost ~5 percent. Consistent with the launch counts: CUDA launches are cheap and this cluster was never host-bound.
l40s_32_cards.probe_is_NOT_valid_as_an_absolute_number: Both arms land far below this cluster's own 724-step steady state (20.08 s median). L40S needs about 100 updates to settle; inside the warm-up the same configuration bounces between 20.5 and 42 s with no trend. Only the within-job on/off difference can be read from these two rows.

points.note: Ascend costs 6 percent more per card-hour, so it must be more than 6 percent faster to win on tokens per point.

historical_baselines_superseded_by_the_r.l40s_production_steady_state: 1506 occupied tokens/s/card over 724 steps, 20.49 s/step, data_wait 0.08

not_measured: Whether the reader fix changes L40S throughput: its data_wait was already 0.08, but its CPUs were doing the same wasted hashing, so the freed capacity may or may not convert.
TorchAIR fusion of the Wan DiT pointwise chain: torch_npu's Dynamo device check reads a None compute capability on this stack. It reaches about 9 percent of launches and cannot touch the remainder.

ascend_production_run.source: live run cq-stage1-8k-npu32 (cqnpu32-hi-001), 32 cards, varlen on, reader fixed

l40s_best_recorded_steady_state.source: run cq-stage1-8k-wsd-32b, 724 measured updates, before the reader fix and before varlen

head_to_head.status: Ascend is ~21 percent faster per card at near-identical cost per card-hour (0.35 vs 0.33 points). A 150-update L40S steady-state measurement with the reader fix, at the configuration that measured best there (varlen off), is running to confirm the L40S side rather than assume it; its first 100 updates are discarded.
